Summary: Moses is the reluctant deliverer: a murderer turned shepherd, called by a burning bush to lead a nation out of slavery. He argued with God, parted a sea, received the law, and never entered the promised land — yet Scripture calls him faithful in all God's house. This character study follows Moses from the Nile to Nebo, so you can learn leadership, obedience, and humility from a man who felt unqualified.
Steps: Read Moses' story in sequence (Exodus 1-20, 32-34, Numbers 11-14, Deuteronomy 31-34), noting his growth and his failures; Study the burning bush (Exodus 3-4) closely, listing Moses' excuses and God's answers to each; Follow the exodus itself (Exodus 5-15), asking what it teaches about God's power and human fear; Study the golden calf (Exodus 32) and Moses' intercession, asking what it means to stand between God and people; End with Deuteronomy 34, reflecting on a life that finished faithful without finishing the journey; Throughout, note Moses' humility (Numbers 12:3) and ask what humble leadership looks like for you
Questions: Why does God choose a reluctant, flawed man to deliver Israel — and what does that say about who he uses?; What do Moses' excuses reveal about your own excuses when God calls you to something hard?; How did Moses handle the people's complaints — and what does that teach about leading people who grumble?; Why did Moses not enter the promised land, and what does that ending teach about faithfulness versus success?; Where is God calling you to step forward despite feeling unqualified?
Application: Name one thing God has been nudging you toward that you have avoided, and take the smallest possible first step this week.
Places: Egypt; Mount Sinai; Plains of Moab
RelatedEvents: The Burning Bush; The Ten Plagues; The Exodus and Crossing of the Red Sea; Giving of the Law at Sinai; Wilderness Wanderings
